subject: chemistry

moments.title: Rabi's molecular beam
moments.body: Rabi detects nuclear magnetic resonance in molecular beams. He wins the 1944 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: NMR is born as a precision atomic-physics technique.

moments.title: NMR in liquids and solids
moments.body: Bloch and Purcell independently detect NMR in liquids (water) and solids (paraffin). They share the 1952 Nobel.

moments.title: Chemical shift discovered
moments.body: Different nuclei in different chemical environments resonate at slightly different frequencies. NMR becomes a fingerprint for organic chemistry. Spin-spin coupling reveals connectivity.
moments.takeaway: NMR is the structural workhorse of organic chemistry.

moments.title: FT-NMR and MRI
moments.who: Richard Ernst, Kurt Wüthrich, Paul Lauterbur, Peter Mansfield
moments.body: Ernst introduces Fourier-transform NMR (1991 Nobel). Wüthrich uses NMR to solve protein structures (2002 Nobel). Lauterbur and Mansfield invent MRI (2003 Nobel).
moments.takeaway: NMR earns at least four Nobel Prizes across physics, chemistry and medicine.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: NMR is ubiquitous in chemistry, biochemistry and medicine. MRI scanners use it for non-invasive imaging. Modern NMR magnets reach 28 tesla; cryogen-free NMR is emerging.
now.open_questions: Can in-cell NMR resolve native protein dynamics? Can hyperpolarised MRI image metabolism in real time?

reflection: NMR began as obscure atomic physics and became a hospital scanner. How often does pure physics become medicine within a generation?
